English-taught degrees are common in countries such as the Netherlands and Germany. - **Turkey:** your route depends on your citizenship and where you completed secondary school. Many Turkish universities accept A Level results in their international student admissions, often with minimum grades, while most Turkish citizens who finished school in Turkey enter through the national exam (YKS, run by ÖSYM). You may also need a diploma equivalence (denklik) from the Ministry of National Education. Check with the university and official sources before you rely on A Levels alone. ## Your 2026–27 timeline | When | What happens (2027 entry) | |---|---| | Summer 2026 (passed) | UCAT testing; LNAT booking for Oxford and Cambridge closed 15 September; UAT-UK October booking closed in late September | | October 2026 | ESAT, TMUA and TARA: 12–16 October. UCAS and LNAT deadline for Oxford, Cambridge and medicine: 15 October. January UAT-UK booking opens late October | | November 2026 | Interview invitations; UCAT results reach universities; prepare for interviews | | December 2026 | Oxford and Cambridge interviews; LNAT deadline for KCL, LSE and UCL: 31 December; booking for the January UAT-UK sitting closes | | January 2027 | ESAT, TMUA and TARA: 4–8 January. UCAS equal-consideration deadline: 13 January. Oxford and Cambridge decisions usually arrive by the end of the month. LNAT deadline for most universities: 25 January | | February–March 2027 | Offers arrive; medical school interviews continue; UCAS Extra opens in late February | | April–May 2027 | Reply to offers (firm and insurance) by your deadline; arrange finance, scholarships and visas; final revision; May/June exams begin | | June 2027 | Final exams; STEP for Cambridge Mathematics offers; end of June: last date to apply before Clearing | | July–August 2027 | Clearing; results in mid-August; places confirmed | | September 2027 | University begins. If you are applying next year instead, UCAT testing for 2028 entry is in the summer | :::quiz ? What is the UCAS deadline for applications to Oxford, Cambridge and most medicine courses for 2027 entry? + 15 October 2026 - 13 January 2027 - 15 September 2026 - 31 December 2026 > Oxford, Cambridge, medicine, dentistry and veterinary courses have the early 15 October deadline. 13 January is the main equal-consideration deadline for most other courses. ? Which statement about the new UCAS personal statement is correct? - It is one free essay of up to 4,000 words + It has three questions, a 4,000-character total and at least 350 characters per answer - You write a different statement for each university - It has five questions, one for each choice > From 2026 entry onwards there are three questions sharing 4,000 characters, each answer at least 350 characters, and all choices see the same statement. ? Which admissions test replaced the MAT for Oxford applicants? - ESAT + TMUA - TARA - STEP > Oxford now uses the TMUA for courses that used the MAT, the ESAT in place of the PAT, and the TARA in place of the TSA. ::: :::recap - UCAS allows up to five choices (at most four in medicine, dentistry or veterinary courses), and normally not both Oxford and Cambridge. - 2027 entry deadlines: 15 October 2026 for Oxford, Cambridge, medicine, dentistry and veterinary courses; 13 January 2027 for most others. - The personal statement has three questions, 4,000 characters in total and at least 350 per answer. Be specific, reflect, and write it yourself. - Your reference and predicted grades come from a teacher or tutor who knows your work. - Choose a firm and an insurance offer; use Extra and Clearing if needed. - Admissions tests: ESAT, TMUA and TARA (12–16 October 2026 or 4–8 January 2027; most Oxford and Cambridge applicants sit in October), UCAT (summer before applying), LNAT (deadlines by university) and STEP (June). - Interviews test thinking aloud; supercurricular activities and the EPQ show genuine interest. - Outside the UK, rules differ by country and university, so check each one; in Turkey, your route depends on citizenship and schooling. ::: Back to the start of the road: [The preparation road at a glance](#road.overview).

#!/usr/bin/env python3 """Widget test harness. Usage: python3 tools/wtest.py src/widgets-math.js 'graph|data-fns="x^2-4" data-x="-5,5" data-y="-5,10"' 'normal|data-mu="0"' ... Options (env): WT_SUBJ=math (subject colour), WT_OUT=/path/prefix (default scratchpad/wtest) Builds a test page with the real stylesheet + src/core.js + the given widget file(s), renders each widget, then takes screenshots: -desk-light.png (1000px) , -phone-dark.png (390px), and prints any console errors / exceptions. Look at the PNGs with your image-reading tool. """ import os, sys, html from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))) SCR = os.environ.get('SCRATCH', __import__('tempfile').gettempdir()) os.makedirs(SCR, exist_ok=True) args = sys.argv[1:] jsfiles = [a for a in args if a.endswith('.js')] specs = [a for a in args if not a.endswith('.js')] subj = os.environ.get('WT_SUBJ', 'math') prefix = os.environ.get('WT_OUT', os.path.join(SCR, 'wtest')) css = open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'src/style.css')).read() core = open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'src/core.js')).read() wjs = '\n;\n'.join(open(os.path.join(ROOT, f) if not os.path.isabs(f) else f).read() for f in jsfiles) items = [] for s in specs: name, _, attrs = s.partition('|') items.append(f'

{html.escape(name)}

') page = f'''
{''.join(items)}
''' path = prefix + '.html' open(path, 'w').write(page) with sync_playwright() as p: b = p.chromium.launch() for tag, w, h, scheme in (('desk-light', 1000, 900, 'light'), ('phone-dark', 390, 844, 'dark')): pg = b.new_page(viewport={'width': w, 'height': h}, color_scheme=scheme) msgs = [] pg.on('console', lambda m: msgs.append(f'{m.type}: {m.text}') if m.type in ('error', 'warning') else None) pg.on('pageerror', lambda e: msgs.append(f'PAGEERROR: {e}')) pg.goto('file://' + path) pg.wait_for_timeout(600) out = f'{prefix}-{tag}.png' pg.screenshot(path=out, full_page=True) sw = pg.evaluate('document.documentElement.scrollWidth') print(f'{out} (page width {sw}px for viewport {w}px{" — OVERFLOW!" if sw > w else ""})') for m in msgs[:20]: print(' ', m) pg.close() b.close() print('test page:', path)
files.tools/svgplot.py: #!/usr/bin/env python3 """House-style SVG graph generator for the guide. Example: python3 tools/svgplot.py --f "x**2-2*x-3" --x -3 5 --y -5 7 --pt "-1,0,(−1, 0)" --pt "3,0,(3, 0)" \ --pt "1,-4,vertex (1, −4)" --vline 1 --caption "The graph of y = x² − 2x − 3" --label "y = x² − 2x − 3" Prints a snippet. Paste it inside a :::html block. Functions use Python syntax with math names available (sin, cos, tan, exp, log, sqrt, pi, e, abs). Classes used (styled by the page, theme-aware): ax, gr, c1, c2, c3, c4, ln, dash, f1, f2, tl, ts, tc, te, ti. """ import argparse, math ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument('--f', action='append', default=[], help='function of x (python syntax); repeatable') ap.add_argument('--label', action='append', default=[], help='legend/curve label for each --f, in order') ap.add_argument('--x', nargs=2, type=float, default=[-5, 5]) ap.add_argument('--y', nargs=2, type=float, default=[-5, 5]) ap.add_argument('--w', type=int, default=560) ap.add_argument('--h', type=int, default=320) ap.add_argument('--xstep', type=float, default=None, help='tick spacing on x (default auto)') ap.add_argument('--ystep', type=float, default=None) ap.add_argument('--nogrid', action='store_true') ap.add_argument('--noticks', action='store_true', help='hide numeric tick labels (sketch style)') ap.add_argument('--pt', action='append', default=[], help='"x,y,label" marks a point; label optional') ap.add_argument('--vline', action='append', default=[], type=float, help='dashed vertical line x=…') ap.add_argument('--hline', action='append', default=[], type=float, help='dashed horizontal line y=…') ap.add_argument('--shade', default=None, help='"f_index,a,b" shade area under curve f between x=a and x=b (index from 0)') ap.add_argument('--xlabel', default='x') ap.add_argument('--ylabel', default='y') ap.add_argument('--caption', default='') ap.add_argument('--legend', default='tr', help='tr or tl') ap.add_argument('--alt', default='') ap.add_argument('--deg', action='store_true', help='x in degrees for trig functions') a = ap.parse_args() W, H = a.w, a.h ml, mr, mt, mb = 34, 18, 14, 26 x0, x1 = a.x; y0, y1 = a.y def px(x): return ml + (x - x0) / (x1 - x0) * (W - ml - mr) def py(y): return mt + (y1 - y) / (y1 - y0) * (H - mt - mb) def nice(span): raw = span / 8 mag = 10 ** math.floor(math.log10(raw)) for m in (1, 2, 2.5, 5, 10): if raw <= m * mag: return m * mag return 10 * mag xs = a.xstep or nice(x1 - x0) ys = a.ystep or nice(y1 - y0) def fmt(v): if abs(v) < 1e-9: return '0' s = ('%.4f' % v).rstrip('0').rstrip('.') return s.replace('-', '−') env = {k: getattr(math, k) for k in dir(math) if not k.startswith('_')} env['abs'] = abs if a.deg: for fn in ('sin', 'cos', 'tan'): env[fn] = (lambda f: (lambda t: f(math.radians(t))))(getattr(math, fn)) out = [] out.append(f'') print(''.join(out))

# BRIEF — writing a Zero to A* chapter (lean edition) Readers are complete beginners aged 15–19; many study alone and many speak English as a second language. Goal: take them from zero to A*-level exam answers. Cambridge International is the main board; put Edexcel International (IAL), AQA and OCR differences in one `:::board` box. ## The file One chapter per file: content//.md. Start with these lines, one per line: @chapter math.p1.functions @title Functions @level as @paper CAIE P1 · Edexcel IAL P2 · UK Pure Year 1 @time 5–7 hours @summary One or two plain sentences. May contain \(x^2\). @level is one of: pre (foundations), as, a2, "as a2", guide, ref, sum, ext. Take the id and title from OUTLINE.md (titles there are final). Link other chapters as [Quadratics](#math.p1.quadratics), only to ids in OUTLINE.md. ## Size (hard limits) | Chapter type | Words | Worked examples | Try-it | Quiz | Figures | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Main-subject topic | 1,300–2,000 | 3 (the last one exam style with marks) | 5 | 3 | ≤ 1 hand SVG; `:::plot` as needed | | Foundations (pre) | 1,200–1,800 | 3–4 | 5 | 3 | ≤ 1 | | Course map (guide) | 600–900 | 0 | 0 | 0–2 | 0 | | Economics / Accounting | 1,000–1,500 | 2 | 4 | 3 | ≤ 1 | | Other-subjects summary | about 250 per subject | – | – | – | – | ## Order inside a topic chapter 1. `:::why` (2–3 sentences: why it matters) 2. "Before you start" with links to prerequisites (optional, one line) 3. 3–6 `##` sections, each: plain-English idea → `:::def` cards for key terms (exam-quality wording) → rules in `:::key` boxes (these also build the formula sheets) → `:::eg` worked examples 4. One or two `:::warn` (common mistakes) and one `:::exam` (exam technique) where they fit 5. `:::board` (2–4 lines, only if boards differ) 6. `:::try` (5 questions, easy → exam style; answers = key steps and the final answer) 7. `:::quiz` (3 questions) 8. `:::recap` (5–7 bullets), then "Next: [title](#id)" In Business and Economics, worked examples are model answers built step by step (knowledge → application → analysis → evaluation), plus calculations where the topic has them. ## Syntax - Inline maths `\( … \)`, display maths `\[ … \]`. Never `$…$` for maths ($ is just a dollar sign). Units upright with thin spaces: `\(9.81\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\)`. Multi-line: `\begin{aligned} a &= b \\ c &= d \end{aligned}`. - Chemistry: `\(\ce{2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O}\)`, `\(\ce{Cu^2+(aq)}\)`, `\(\ce{CH3COOH <=> CH3COO- + H+}\)`. - Vectors: `\mathbf{a}`, `\overrightarrow{AB}`, `\begin{pmatrix}3\\-1\end{pmatrix}`. Never \vec, \overline, \cancel, \boxed. - Blocks: a line `:::type Title` at column 0, a line `:::` to close, blank lines around. Types: def, eg, key, formula, tip, warn, exam, analogy, why, board, lab, note, steps, cols + col, try, quiz, recap, html, plot. - Exam marks inside `:::eg`, written separately: `[M1] [A1] [B1]` (method, accuracy, independent). - `:::try`: a line starting `Q:` begins a question, `A:` its answer; further lines continue them. - `:::quiz`: `? question`, options `+ correct` (exactly one) and `- wrong`, then `> explanation`. - Tables: Markdown pipes. Bold a key word the first time if it has no `:::def` card. ## Figures, cheapest first 1. Graphs of functions: a `:::plot` block. The build draws it; you write one line of options. :::plot The parabola y = x² − 2x − 3 crosses the x-axis at −1 and 3. --f "x**2-2*x-3" --x -3 5 --y -5 7 --pt "1,-4,vertex (1, −4)@e" --vline 1 --label "y = x² − 2x − 3" --legend tl ::: Options: several --f (Python syntax: x**2, sin(x), exp(x), log(x), sqrt(x)); --x a b; --y a b; --pt "x,y,label@dir" (dir n s e w ne nw se sw); --vline; --hline; --shade "0,a,b"; --deg; --noticks; --nogrid; --xlabel; --ylabel; --label (one per --f); --legend tl|tr. Straight lines draw economics diagrams (use --noticks and point labels). 2. Only when a picture is essential (force diagram, circuit, cell, apparatus, mechanism): ONE small hand SVG (40 elements at most) inside `:::html`: `` Classes only, never colours. Lines: ln, ln-m, c1, c2, c3, ax (+ dash, thin, thick). Fills (every filled shape needs one): f1, f2, f3, fm, fi, fa, fp. Text: tl, ts, tb, ti, tc, te, ta, tr, halo. Arrows: marker-end="url(#ah)" (also #ahr, #ah-). No ids, defs, markers, styles or images. 3. Widgets, at most one per chapter, inside `:::html`: `
`. graph (data-fns="a*x^2+b; 2x" data-x="-6,6" data-y="-5,10" data-params="a=1,-3,3,0.1"), unitcircle, stats (data-values), normal (data-mu data-sigma data-a data-b), binomial (data-n data-p), projectile (data-g data-speed data-angle), wave (data-mode=single|superpose|stationary), halflife (data-n0 data-half), units, periodic, molar (data-formula), ohm, punnett (data-cross="Aa x Aa"), chisq, supplydemand, breakeven (data-fc data-price data-vc), npv, ratios, planner, timer, ucas. ## Accuracy - Recompute every number (examples, answers, quiz options) in the chapter's single python check. - Cambridge values: Physics g = 9.81 m s⁻²; Maths mechanics g = 10; c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹; e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C; h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s; N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹; R = 8.31 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹; F = 9.65 × 10⁴ C mol⁻¹; molar gas volume 24.0 dm³ mol⁻¹ at room conditions; water 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹. Maths answers to 3 significant figures unless exact. - Exam facts (papers, durations, weightings, admissions tests) only from PLAN.md. Never invent dates, fees or paper details; if unsure, leave it out. - Original wording and original questions only. Never copy past papers or textbooks. ## Style British English (colour, analyse, sulfur, aluminium). Short sentences, "you", warm and direct. Define every new term. No emojis, no filler phrases, no em-dash asides, no hype.

# WP0 — one-time engine upgrade (run before any content package)

Goal: make every later session cheap. Work in /home/claude/zta after the normal session start
(SESSION.md). Read build.js, lib.js, tools/check.js and tools/make_outline.py before editing (they are
short). Change them with Edit or small python patches, not full rewrites.

## 1. One chapter per file
- New chapters live in content/<subject>/<chapter-id>.md.
- build.js: find chapters by globbing content/**/*.md (recursive), render every file, then order and group
  chapters from src/outline.json (subject order, chapter order, group titles). Ignore @group lines. Keep the
  existing multi-chapter files working (home.md, start.md, roadmap-1.md, roadmap-2.md, math-1a.md,
  tools.md, practice.md); do not split or delete them. Replace the "missing files" message with a count of
  outline chapters not written yet.
- A chapter id that is not in the outline (after alias resolution) is an error; duplicate ids are errors.
- tools/check.js: accept any file under content/; validate each chapter id against the outline and aliases;
  drop the "expected chapters in this file" and order checks.

## 2. Merges and aliases
Edit tools/make_outline.py: remove the absorbed ids, give each surviving chapter its new title, add an
`aliases` map (old id → surviving id) to outline.json, then run it (it also regenerates OUTLINE.md,
including an Aliases section).

| Surviving id | New title | Absorbs |
|---|---|---|
| math.f.numbers | Numbers, powers, surds and standard form | math.f.powers |
| math.f.graphs | Graphs, geometry and trigonometry basics | math.f.geometry |
| phys.temperature | Thermal physics: temperature, ideal gases and thermodynamics | phys.gases, phys.thermo |
| chem.lattice | Lattice energy, entropy and Gibbs free energy | chem.entropy |
| bio.classification | Classification, biodiversity, conservation and ecosystems | bio.ecology |
| eng.overview | Engineering: routes, careers and course map | eng.what |
| eng.materials | Materials, stress and beams | eng.mechanics |
| eng.electronics | Electronics, digital systems and control | eng.control |
| bus.enterprise | Enterprise, business structure and size | bus.structure, bus.size |
| bus.hrm | Human resource management and management | bus.management |
| bus.marketing | Marketing and market research | bus.research |
| bus.operations | Operations, inventory, capacity and outsourcing | bus.inventory |
| bus.finance | Business finance, sources of finance and cash flow | bus.cashflow |
| bus.org | Organisation, communication, leadership and HRM strategy | bus.leadership |
| econ.firms | Costs, market structures and labour markets | econ.labour |
| econ.trade | Trade, exchange rates, development and globalisation | econ.development |
| acc.basics | Double entry, reconciliations and errors | acc.control |
| acc.statements | Financial statements and their analysis | acc.analysis |
| other.cs | Computer Science, Psychology and other sciences | other.psychology, other.pe, other.more |
| other.english | Humanities, languages and the arts | other.history, other.geography, other.sociology, other.law, other.politics, other.languages, other.arts, other.humanities |

build.js rewrites links href="#old" and href="#old--section" to "#new" before checking links; check.js
treats aliases as valid. The outline's "file"/"owner" fields are no longer used.

## 3. `:::plot` block
In lib.js add block type `plot` (and add it to BLOCK_TYPES): title = caption; body = one line of
tools/svgplot.py options. Split the options like a shell does (support "double-quoted" strings), run
`python3 tools/svgplot.py <options> --caption <title>` with child_process.execFileSync (cwd = project root)
and use stdout as the block's HTML. On failure record a checker error with the last line of stderr.

## 4. Automatic formula sheets
In lib.js, when rendering `:::key` and `:::formula` blocks, also push {chapter, title, html} to a new st.KEYS
list. In build.js, for each chapter tools.f.<x>, append after its body, for every chapter of the mapped
subject(s) in outline order that has KEYS: "## <chapter title>", its boxes, and a link "Revise: <chapter title>".
Map: tools.f.math→math, tools.f.phys→phys, tools.f.chem→chem, tools.f.bio→bio, tools.f.eng→eng,
tools.f.bus→bus and econ. Create content/tools/tools.f.<x>.md for all six (header lines from OUTLINE.md and
a 2–3 sentence intro saying Cambridge prints a formula or data list in the exam, but you must know when
and how to use each formula).

## 5. Check and finish
- `node build.js --warn | tail -n 20` → 0 errors. Run tools/check.js on an existing file and on a throwaway
  sample chapter that uses :::plot (delete the sample afterwards).
- Normal end-of-session steps (publish + commit). Also commit every changed engine file: build.js, lib.js,
  tools/check.js, tools/make_outline.py, src/outline.json, OUTLINE.md and content/tools/*.md.
- Write "DONE WP0" in the STATUS.md line.

# Zero to A* — author's guide (read all of this before writing) You are writing chapters for **Zero to A\***, a free, single-page interactive A Level course. It is aimed at a student who knows **nothing** about the subject yet (many readers are self-studying, aged 15–19, and many speak English as a second language, e.g. in Turkey), and it must take them all the way to **top-grade exam standard**. The main reference board is **Cambridge International (CAIE)**; wherever Pearson Edexcel (International A Level, IAL), AQA or OCR differ, say so. The finished site is built from Markdown files in `content/` by `node build.js`. You only write your own content files. **Never edit** `build.js`, `lib.js`, anything in `src/`, `tools/`, or another author's content file. Never run `node build.js` (it overwrites shared output). Validate with the checker instead (see "Checking your work"). The gold-standard example of a finished chapter is **`content/math-1a.md` (Quadratics)**. Read it first, and match its tone, structure and formatting. The list of valid chapter ids is in **`OUTLINE.md`** (read that, not `src/outline.json`). ### SAVE YOUR WORK AS YOU GO (critical) The machine can be stopped at any moment. Work that exists only in your head or in a scratch file is lost. **Write each chapter into your content file as soon as it is drafted** (the first chapter with the Write tool; every later chapter appended, e.g. with a short `python3` append or the Edit tool), then run the checker. Never draft several chapters before saving, and never assemble the file only at the end. A finished chapter on disk is worth more than a perfect plan. Keep thinking brief and spend your effort on the chapters themselves. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## 1. Pedagogy: what every chapter must do 1. **Start from zero.** Open with the idea in plain English and a real-world hook (why it matters). Assume the reader has only basic school maths/science unless a "Before you start" link says otherwise. Define every technical word the first time it appears (in a `:::def` card for important terms, inline for minor ones). 2. **Build up in small steps.** Intuition → precise definition → rule/formula → worked examples (easy → exam level) → common mistakes → exam technique. Use analogies (`:::analogy`) where a concept is abstract. 3. **Reach real A Level depth.** Cover everything the Cambridge syllabus lists for the topic (and note extra content that Edexcel/AQA/OCR include). A student who masters the chapter should be able to answer real exam questions. 4. **Worked examples are the heart.** At least 3–5 per substantial chapter, graded in difficulty. Show every step, with reasons. The last one or two should be "exam style" with mark annotations `[M1]` `[A1]` `[B1]` placed where an examiner would award them (M = method, A = accuracy, dependent on M, B = independent mark). For essay subjects (Business, Economics), worked examples are model answers / paragraph builds showing knowledge → application → analysis → evaluation. 5. **Practice with full answers.** End each substantial chapter with a `:::try` block of 6–10 questions that ramp from easy to exam standard, each with a complete worked answer (not just the final number). 6. **Quick check.** Then a `:::quiz` with 3–6 multiple-choice questions (exactly one correct option, 3–5 options, plausible distractors that reflect real misconceptions, and an explanation line). 7. **Summary.** Finish with a `:::recap` of 5–9 bullet points: the facts a student must remember. 8. **Connect.** Link to prerequisite and follow-on chapters using the chapter ids in `src/outline.json`, e.g. `[Moles and stoichiometry](#chem.moles)`. Only link to ids that exist in the outline. Guide/overview chapters (course maps, roadmap phases, "other subjects" summaries) are prose-led and do not need `:::try`; they still benefit from tables, `:::tip`, `:::exam`, `:::warn` and a `:::recap`. ### Length (these targets override any longer numbers in a brief) - Main topic chapters: **1,500–2,800 words** of prose, 3–5 worked examples, 5–8 practice questions, 3–4 quiz questions, 1–2 figures. Cover the whole syllabus point concisely; no filler, no repetition. - Course-map / overview chapters: 800–1,400 words. "From zero" foundation chapters: 1,400–2,400 words. - The checker prints a word count per chapter. ### Writing style - **British English** spelling (colour, organise, metre, analyse, programme, sulfur (IUPAC/Cambridge spelling), aluminium). - Short, clear sentences. Active voice. Speak to the reader as "you". Warm and encouraging, never patronising. - No emojis. No filler phrases ("It's worth noting", "In conclusion", "Let's dive in"). No exclamation-mark hype. - Avoid em-dash asides; use commas, colons or new sentences. - Use **bold** for a key word when first introduced (if it is not in a `:::def` card). - Use real units, real data, realistic numbers. Never write lorem ipsum or placeholders. - **Original writing only.** Do not copy text from textbooks, websites or past papers. Write original questions "in the style of" exam questions; do not reproduce real past-paper questions. ### Accuracy (non-negotiable) - **Verify every calculation with Python** (`python3 -c "..."`) before you write the answer. Check rounding and significant figures. Quiz answers must be unambiguous and correct. - Cambridge conventions: Maths answers to **3 significant figures** unless exact; angles in degrees to 1 d.p. **Cambridge 9709 Mechanics uses g = 10 m s⁻²** (state "take g = 10"); Edexcel uses 9.8; **Physics 9702 uses g = 9.81 m s⁻²**. Physics/Chemistry data values must match the Cambridge data sheets (e.g. e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹, R = 8.31 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, F = 9.65 × 10⁴ C mol⁻¹, molar gas volume 24.0 dm³ mol⁻¹ at room conditions, specific heat capacity of water 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹). - Use the syllabus's own terminology and definitions where they exist (e.g. "water potential", "standard enthalpy change of formation", "electromotive force"). If you are not sure of a fact, leave it out rather than guess. - Board facts verified in Oct 2026 are in `PLAN.md` (paper structures etc.). Do not invent exam dates or fees. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## 2. File format A content file is Markdown with a few extensions. It contains one or more chapters. ``` @group Pure Mathematics 1 <- sidebar group heading (use the group named in your brief) @chapter math.p1.functions <- chapter id: EXACTLY as in your brief / src/outline.json @title Functions @level as <- start | pre | as | a2 | "as a2" | guide | tool | ref | sum | ext @paper CAIE P1 · Edexcel IAL P2 · AQA/OCR/Edexcel Pure <- where it is examined (short) @time 5–7 hours <- realistic study time for a beginner @summary One or two sentences: what the chapter covers, in plain English. May contain \(maths\). ...chapter body... @chapter math.p1.coord <- next chapter starts ... ``` - The `@` lines must be at the very top of each chapter, one per line, before any body text. - Write `@group` only when the group changes (it applies to following chapters). Chapters must appear in the order given in your brief. - The chapter title is the only `

`. In the body use `##` for sections and `###` for subsections (`####` rarely). - Levels: `pre` = foundations below A Level; `as` = AS (first year); `a2` = A Level second year; `as a2` if a chapter spans both (mark the A2 part clearly inside with a heading or a `:::note A Level only`). ### Maths and science notation - Inline maths: `\( ... \)` Display maths: `\[ ... \]` (KaTeX/LaTeX syntax). **Never use `$`** for maths. Dollar signs are literal text (prices in Business/Economics are fine: "$4.50"). - Use maths markup for every formula, variable and unit-with-number in technical text: `\(v = u + at\)`, `\(3.0 \times 10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\)`, `\(x^2\)`. Upright units with `\mathrm{}` and a thin space `\,`. - Chemistry: use mhchem inside maths delimiters: `\(\ce{H2SO4}\)`, `\(\ce{2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O}\)`, `\(\ce{CH3COOH <=> CH3COO- + H+}\)`, `\(\ce{Fe^3+}\)`, `\(\ce{Cu^2+(aq)}\)`, state symbols `\(\ce{NaCl(s)}\)`. `\ce{->[\text{heat}]}` for conditions over an arrow. - Vectors: bold `\mathbf{a}`, or `\overrightarrow{AB}`, or column vectors `\begin{pmatrix}3\\-1\end{pmatrix}`. Do not use `\vec{}` or `\overline{}` (they render poorly). Avoid `\cancel`, `\boxed`, `\bbox`. - Multi-line working: `\begin{aligned} ... &= ... \\ ... &= ... \end{aligned}` inside `\[ \]`. - Units in prose without numbers can be plain text ("measured in newtons, N"). ### Blocks Blocks start with `:::type Optional title` on its own line **at column 0** and end with a line containing only `:::`. Leave a blank line before and after each block. Blocks may contain Markdown, maths, tables and lists. | Block | Use it for | |---|---| | `:::def Term` | A key term with its exact definition (shown as an index card; also feeds the glossary). One term per card. Title = the term. Body = the definition (1–3 sentences, examiner-quality wording). | | `:::eg Title` | A worked example. Title = the question. Body = full solution. Use `[M1] [A1] [B1]` marks for exam-style ones. | | `:::key Title` | Key facts / formulas to memorise (shown like a formula booklet box). | | `:::formula Title` | A single important formula with its symbols explained. | | `:::tip Title` | A helpful technique or shortcut. | | `:::warn Title` | A common mistake and how to avoid it (red-pen box). | | `:::exam Title` | Exam technique: what the question wants, where the marks are, command words. | | `:::analogy` | An everyday analogy for an abstract idea. | | `:::why` | Why this topic matters (use once, at the start). | | `:::board` | Differences between Cambridge, Edexcel (IAL), AQA, OCR for this topic. | | `:::lab Title` | Practical/required-practical notes (method, apparatus, safety, sources of error). | | `:::note Title` / `:::story Title` / `:::career Title` | Asides: extra info, history of an idea, where it leads. | | `:::steps` | A numbered procedure (write a normal `1.` `2.` list inside). | | `:::cols` containing `:::col Title` blocks | Side-by-side comparison (e.g. mitosis vs meiosis). | | `:::try Title` | Practice questions. Lines starting `Q:` begin a question, `A:` begins its answer. Continuation lines follow. | | `:::quiz Title` | MCQs. `? question`, `+ correct option`, `- wrong option`, `> explanation`. Exactly one `+` per question. | | `:::recap` | End-of-chapter summary bullets. | | `:::html` | Raw HTML passed through unchanged: **use this for every SVG figure and every widget**. | `:::try` format example: ``` :::try Q: Solve \(x^2 - 9 = 0\). A: \(x^2 = 9\), so \(x = 3\) or \(x = -3\). Q: (Exam style) A second question can have several lines, including display maths: \[y = 2x + 1\] A: Full worked answer here. [M1] Second line of the answer. [A1] ::: ``` `:::quiz` format example: ``` :::quiz ? Which particle has a negative charge? - proton + electron - neutron > Electrons carry a charge of −1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C; protons are positive and neutrons are neutral. ::: ``` ### Tables GitHub-style Markdown tables are encouraged for comparisons, data, and "AS vs A2" maps. Keep cells short. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## 3. Diagrams (inline SVG) Good diagrams matter: aim for **1–3 SVG figures per main chapter** where a picture explains the mechanism (force diagrams, circuits, wave patterns, cells and organelles, the heart, apparatus, energy-level diagrams, graphs, supply/demand diagrams, organisational charts, flowcharts). Only draw what is accurate. Wrap each figure in a `:::html` block: ``` :::html ::: ``` Rules (the page restyles these classes for light and dark mode, so **never hard-code colours**: no `fill="#..."`, `stroke="red"` or `style="color..."`): - **No `id` attributes, no ``, no ``, no `

# Zero to A* — plan for finishing the project economically

*Written 1 October 2026 at the end of the setup sessions. This is the master plan for you, the owner. Each Claude work session follows the shorter **SESSION.md** (procedure) and **BRIEF.md** (how to write a chapter) instead of reading this file.*

---

## Start here: how to continue

1. In the Claude app, start a **new task** (do not continue the old conversation) and connect this folder, **Zero to A**.
2. If the app lets you pick a model, choose **Sonnet** for writing packages. It does this job well and uses your limit far more slowly than Opus. Keep Opus for untangling problems.
3. Paste this prompt:

> Continue my Zero to A* project. The folder "Zero to A" is connected. Stage SESSION.md, STATUS.md, dist\backup.json, vendor\node_modules.tgz and vendor\latinmodern-math.otf from it, read SESSION.md and follow it exactly to run the next work package. No clarifying questions, no task list, no subagents, no web searches (one syllabus fetch is fine). Commit every chapter to my folder, publish at the end, then stop and report in three lines.

4. When it reports back, glance at your usage meter. Then start another new task with the same prompt for the next package. **One package per task.**

The first package (WP0) upgrades the engine so every later package is cheap. Run it first.

---

## 1. Where the project stands

| | |
|---|---|
| Published page | **Zero to A\*** (private until you share it): https://claude.ai/artifact/V8KUdftuzroYvq7cp4KPWd, version 2 |
| Offline copy | `dist/zero-to-a-star.html` in this folder opens in any browser |
| Finished pages (27) | Home; Start Here (5 chapters); Preparation Roadmap (15 chapters, including the study-plan generator); Quadratics (the model chapter); Toolbox page shells (4); Practice page |
| Finished widgets (6) | Graph plotter, unit circle, statistics, **study planner**, Pomodoro timer, UCAS calculator |
| Engine | Markdown → one self-contained web page. Formulas render as real maths, light "exam paper" and dark "chalkboard" themes, search, progress tracking, glossary and practice quizzes built automatically |
| Still to do | 168 chapters in 28 content packages, 15 widgets in 3 packages, a one-time engine upgrade (WP0) and a final quality pass (WP32) |

---

## 2. Why it cost so much, and what changes

| What drove the cost | What happened | From now on |
|---|---|---|
| One very long conversation | The old conversation carries all the code, styling, research and agent instructions. Every single step re-reads all of it. | Each package runs in a **fresh, short conversation** that reads only SESSION.md and BRIEF.md (about 4,000 words together). |
| Many agents at once | 15 agents in parallel emptied the limit in minutes. Five agents used a whole window for 20 chapters and 6 widgets. | **No agents.** One conversation writes its own package, one chapter at a time. |
| Agent overhead | Each agent first read about 40,000 tokens of instructions, then took 55–70 steps, and its memory grew at every step. | **3 steps per chapter**: write it, check it, save it. |
| Most expensive model | Every agent ran on Opus. | **Sonnet** for writing. |
| Lost work | After the first limit hit, the cloud machine restarted. Drafts that had not been saved yet vanished (about 2.9 million tokens of work). | **Every finished chapter goes straight into this folder.** Nothing waits until the end of a session. |
| Heavy chapters | 2,500–4,000 words, 8–10 practice questions, hand-drawn diagrams. A single plotted graph is about 2,000 tokens of drawing code. | 1,300–2,000 words, 5 practice questions. **Graphs are generated from one line of text at build time.** Formula sheets are assembled automatically from each chapter's key-facts boxes. |
| Checking with screenshots | Rendering pages and reading images is expensive. | The automatic checker does the checking. Screenshots only for new widgets and in the final QA. |
| Long instructions per agent | Each agent got a long hand-written brief. | Each package fetches the **official Cambridge syllabus** once and uses its learning outcomes as the checklist. This is cheaper and more accurate. |

---

## 3. The new method in one paragraph

A work session restores the project from this folder into the cloud workbench (one small transfer), reads the two short manuals, and fetches the syllabus outcomes for its topics. It then writes each chapter in **one go**, runs the checker and a one-call numeric check, and **saves that chapter to this folder immediately**. At the end it builds the page, publishes it to the same link, saves the built files and a full backup here, adds one line to STATUS.md, and stops. A package is 4–8 chapters, so even if a limit hits mid-package you lose at most the chapter being written. `tools/status.py` always shows what is done and what comes next.

---

## 4. Scope: what stays, what is trimmed

**Kept in full:**
- **The six main subjects** (Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Engineering, Business) cover the whole Cambridge syllabus. Every topic chapter keeps the plain-English start, key-term cards, 3 worked examples (the last one marked like an exam), common mistakes, an exam tip, board differences, 5 practice questions with answers, 3 quick-check questions and a summary.
- Accuracy rules: Cambridge data values, every number re-computed, syllabus checklist per package.

**Trimmed:**
- **Chapter length.** Topic chapters are 1,300–2,000 words (was 2,500–4,000). Course maps are 600–900 words.
- **Economics and Accounting** (the business-related extras) are compact: 1,000–1,500 words.
- **Other subjects** become 3 summary chapters with about 250 words per subject, which is what you asked for.
- **20 merges of small neighbouring topics** (232 planned pages → 201), for example "Temperature", "Ideal gases" and "Thermodynamics" become one "Thermal physics" chapter. Old links keep working through aliases. The full list is in WP0.md.
- **Formula sheets** are generated automatically instead of written by hand.
- **Two minor widgets dropped** (resistor colour code, Hardy–Weinberg). Both calculations stay in the text.

---

## 5. The work packages

Packages run in this order. `tools/wp.json` holds the exact chapter list for each, and `python3 tools/status.py` shows progress.

| **WP0** | Engine upgrade: one file per chapter, merges and aliases, one-line graphs, automatic formula sheets | setup |

---

## 6. Budget and pacing

**What will it cost?** We will know after WP0 and WP1. The old method used about one full usage window for 20 chapters. The new one cuts cost in four ways at once: a cheaper model, about a third of the steps per chapter, much smaller conversations, and shorter chapters. Expect **at least three times as many chapters per window**, likely more. At three times, that is about 60 chapters per window: roughly three windows for the 168 chapters, plus one for widgets and the final pass. These are estimates, not promises.

**Calibrate once.** Note your usage meter before and after WP0 and WP1. If a package costs X% of a window, you can run about **85 ÷ X** packages per window and still stop before 100%.

**Stop rule.** If you are near your limit, type "usage is high". The session finishes the current chapter, saves it, publishes, and stops.

---

## 7. Safeguards

- **This folder is the master copy.** Every chapter is saved here as soon as it is written. Cloud restarts no longer lose work.
- **Two backups.** `dist/backup.json` (all sources in one file) is updated with every chapter, here and inside the published page.
- **Always resumable.** STATUS.md and `tools/status.py` tell any new session exactly where to pick up.
- **Quality gate.** The checker rejects broken maths, wrong formats, bad links and malformed quizzes. Every number is recomputed. The syllabus outcomes are the coverage checklist. WP32 re-checks a sample of worked examples, looks at the finished page on desktop and phone, and fixes what it finds.
- **The link always works.** Each package ends with a publish to the same address.

---

## 8. If you need it even cheaper

1. **Publish less often.** Publish every third package and read `dist/zero-to-a-star.html` locally in between.
2. **Shorter chapters.** 1,000–1,400 words each.
3. **Fewer widgets.** Keep only normal, binomial, periodic table, formula mass and break-even (saves about two packages).
4. **Do the extras last, or drop them.** Economics, Accounting and Other subjects (WP29–31).
5. **Automate.** Once two packages have gone smoothly by hand, a scheduled task can run the same prompt every few hours and use your limit windows while you are away. Your computer and the Claude app must be on.

---

## 9. What is in this folder

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `HANDOFF.md` | This plan |
| `SESSION.md` | Step-by-step procedure every work session follows |
| `BRIEF.md` | How to write a chapter (short version of AUTHORING.md) |
| `WP0.md` | Spec for the one-time engine upgrade |
| `STATUS.md` | One line per session: what was done, what is next |
| `README.md` | Quick orientation |
| `PLAN.md` | Verified facts (paper structures, admissions tests, dates) checked in October 2026 |
| `OUTLINE.md`, `src/outline.json` | Every chapter id, title, level and group |
| `AUTHORING.md`, `WIDGETS.md` | Full author and widget guides (reference only) |
| `content/` | The chapters (Markdown) |
| `src/` | Page shell, styling, app code, widgets |
| `build.js`, `lib.js` | The builder (Markdown + maths → one web page) |
| `tools/` | Checker, graph generator, progress report, package list, backup, widget tester |
| `dist/index.html` | The built page as published |
| `dist/zero-to-a-star.html` | The same page as a standalone file to open offline |
| `dist/backup.json` | Every source file in one bundle (what sessions restore from) |
| `vendor/` | Maths font and pinned code libraries, so builds do not depend on downloads |

Do not edit `dist/` by hand; it is rebuilt every session.

# SESSION — procedure for every Zero to A* work session

Usage is the scarce resource. Follow this exactly. Read only this file, BRIEF.md and the output of
`python3 tools/status.py`. Do not read HANDOFF.md, AUTHORING.md, src/outline.json or other chapters
unless a step below tells you to.

## Fixed facts
- ROOT (the user's folder, master copy): C:\Users\Uncertainty\Desktop\Claude_Test\Zero to A
- Cloud workbench: /home/claude/zta (rebuilt from ROOT every session)
- Published page: https://claude.ai/artifact/V8KUdftuzroYvq7cp4KPWd (title "Zero to A*")
- There is no shell on the user's PC. Build in the cloud; move files with device_stage_files and
  device_commit_files. Files you commit must first be copied under /mnt/user-data/outputs/zta/.

## Rules
1. One work package per conversation, then stop.
2. No subagents, no parallel agents, no Workflow, no WebSearch, no clarifying questions, no task list.
   One WebFetch of the package's official syllabus is allowed (content packages).
3. Each chapter: ONE Write (the whole chapter) → ONE bash (check, verify numbers, backup, copy) →
   ONE commit. Fix problems with small Edit calls. Never rewrite a chapter to fix a detail and never
   read back a chapter you just wrote.
4. No screenshots in content packages. Widget packages: one tools/wtest.py run per widget; look at the
   phone-dark PNG, and at the desktop PNG only if something seems wrong.
5. Keep tool output short (`| tail -n 20`). Never cat large files.
6. Talk to the user only at the end, in three lines.
7. If the user says usage is high: finish the current chapter, save it, do the end steps, stop.

## Start (4 calls)
1. device_stage_files (one call): ROOT\SESSION.md, ROOT\STATUS.md, ROOT\dist\backup.json,
   ROOT\vendor\node_modules.tgz, ROOT\vendor\latinmodern-math.otf.
   They arrive under "/mnt/user-data/uploads/Zero to A/".
2. One bash:
   U="/mnt/user-data/uploads/Zero to A"; mkdir -p /home/claude/zta && cd /home/claude/zta && python3 -c "import json,os,sys;d=json.load(open(sys.argv[1],encoding='utf-8'))['files'];[(os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p) or '.',exist_ok=True),open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(t)) for p,t in d.items()];print(len(d),'files restored')" "$U/dist/backup.json" && cp "$U/STATUS.md" STATUS.md && mkdir -p vendor && cp "$U/vendor/latinmodern-math.otf" vendor/ && tar xzf "$U/vendor/node_modules.tgz" && (pip install -q brotli --break-system-packages >/dev/null 2>&1 || true) && python3 tools/status.py | tail -n 14
3. Read /home/claude/zta/BRIEF.md. If status.py names a spec file (e.g. WP0.md), read that too.
4. Content packages: one WebFetch of the syllabus URL printed by status.py with the prompt
   "List compactly, as bullets, every learning outcome for <topics>." Use the list as your coverage checklist.

## Each chapter (3 calls)
1. Write /home/claude/zta/content/<subject>/<chapter-id>.md
   (subject = math, phys, chem, bio, eng, bus, econ (also for acc.*), other, tools).
2. One bash (the heredoc recomputes every number in the chapter and prints only failures):
   cd /home/claude/zta && node tools/check.js content/<subject>/<id>.md | tail -n 12 && python3 - <<'PY'
   # e.g. assert abs(10*3.0*math.cos(math.radians(30)) - 26) < 0.5
   print('numbers OK')
   PY
   python3 tools/backup.py >/dev/null && O=/mnt/user-data/outputs/zta && mkdir -p "$O/content/<subject>" "$O/dist" && cp content/<subject>/<id>.md "$O/content/<subject>/" && cp dist/backup.json "$O/dist/"
3. device_commit_files with force: true:
   /mnt/user-data/outputs/zta/content/<subject>/<id>.md → ROOT\content\<subject>\<id>.md
   /mnt/user-data/outputs/zta/dist/backup.json → ROOT\dist\backup.json

## End (4 calls)
1. One bash: cd /home/claude/zta && node build.js | tail -n 6 && python3 tools/backup.py, then append one
   line to STATUS.md: "- <YYYY-MM-DD> · <WP id> · <what was added> · <notes>" (include "DONE <WP id>"
   when the package is complete), then python3 tools/status.py | tail -n 4, then copy dist/index.html,
   dist/zero-to-a-star.html, dist/backup.json and STATUS.md into /mnt/user-data/outputs/zta/ (same sub-paths).
2. Artifact read: url = the published page, path = "backup.json" (this counts as reading the page; the
   file is saved to disk, not printed).
3. Artifact publish: url = the published page, file_path = /home/claude/zta/dist/index.html,
   files = {"backup.json": "/home/claude/zta/dist/backup.json"}, label = "<WP id>". No icon.
4. device_commit_files (force: true): dist\index.html, dist\zero-to-a-star.html, dist\backup.json, STATUS.md.
Then reply in three lines: what was added, anything uncertain, what is next.

## If something goes wrong
- Publish refused because the page was not read: do one plain Artifact read of it (costly, once), then publish.
- Checker says an id is unknown: use an id from OUTLINE.md (or an alias listed there).
- Widget packages: write the file named by status.py in sections, test each widget with
  `WT_OUT=/tmp/wt python3 tools/wtest.py src/<file>.js 'name|data-…'`, commit the file after each widget.
- Engine edits (WP0 or a fix): commit every changed engine file as well.
